newsitem.title: USA: Deere shares drop after Q4 results.
newsitem.headline: Deere shares drop after Q4 results.

text.p: Shares of Deere & Co declined 2-5/8 to 44 after the company reported net earnings for the fiscal fourth quarter that were below expectations.
"Deere came in a little light on a reported basis," NatWest Markets analyst Thomas Burns said.
But on an operating basis, excluding a $15.0 million after-tax write-off related to Mexican operations, Deere's earnings were within the range of expectations, he added.
Deere reported net earnings for the fourth quarter ended October 31 of $0.68 a share, below the First Call mean of $0.75 a share, based on a range of $0.64 to $0.91 a share.
Adding in the approximately $0.05 a share Mexican charge, Deere's earnings would be $0.73 a share and within the range of expectations, Burns said.
Burns said profit-taking, following recent gains in the stock, also contributed to weakness in the shares. Deere closed Monday at 46-5/8, near its 52-week high of 47-1/8.
The analyst said there are also some concerns about the variables in Deere's outlook for next year.
"It's a very busy (outlook) for them. They've got lots of balls in the air to get their earnings and not much in real growth in their markets," Burns said.

These variables, as he called them, include selling agricultural equipment overseas in markets like Kazakhstan, addressing problems in its lawn and garden products, and some reliance on good weather to contribute to overall demand from the agricultural sector.
